properties.name: Indus Valley Civilization (Mature Harappan)
properties.ruler_or_system: Civic Merchant Assemblies / Standardized Urban System
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Boundaries depict the maximum distribution zone of Mature Harappan urban artifacts, town planning, standardized weights, and seal scripts rather than rigid modern political borders.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Kenoyer / Possehl archaeological catalogues
properties.highlights: Grid-pattern urban planning, underground drainage, standardized fired brick ratios (1:2:4), tidal dockyard at Lothal, reservoirs at Dholavira.

properties.name: Sixteen Mahajanapadas (Iron Age Republics & Kingdoms)
properties.capital: Major Capitals: Rajagriha, Vaishali, Kaushambi, Ujjayini, Shravasti
properties.ruler_or_system: Oligarchic Ganasanghas (Vajji, Malla) & Monarchies (Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti)
properties.primary_rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Son, Sarayu, Gandak, Narmada
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Outlines define the primary northern cultural and political realm described in early Buddhist (Anguttara Nikaya) and Jain (Bhagavati Sutra) canonical literature.
properties.citation: Rhys Davids, H.C. Raychaudhuri, R.S. Sharma (Ancient India)
properties.trade_connections: Uttarapatha (Northern Trunk Route) connecting Taxila to Champa & Tamralipti
properties.highlights: Second Urbanization of India, emergence of punch-marked coinage, life of Gautama Buddha and Vardhamana Mahavira.

properties.name: Maurya Empire (Under Emperor Ashoka the Great)
properties.primary_rivers: Ganga, Indus, Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Bound based on the find-spots of Ashoka's Major and Minor Rock Edicts and Pillar Edicts (from Kandahar/Shahbazgarhi to Maski/Brahmagiri). Southern boundary reflects independent friendly Tamil states (Cholas, Pandyas, Cheras) recorded in Rock Edict II.
properties.citation: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum Vol. I (Edicts of Asoka, E. Hultzsch) & ASI Inscription Survey
properties.trade_connections: Trans-continental links to Hellenistic Kingdoms (Egypt, Syria, Macedonia, Cyrene, Epirus)
properties.highlights: First political unification of the subcontinent, Dhamma governance, edicts engraved on rock faces and polished sandstone monoliths, construction of the Grand Trunk precursor.

properties.name: Gupta Empire (Classical Golden Age of India)
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Boundaries derived from the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) composed by Harishena, detailing directly administered zones and southern tributary alliances.
properties.citation: Fleet (Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum Vol. III) & R.C. Majumdar (The Classical Age)
properties.trade_connections: Maritime connections with Southeast Asia (Suvarnabhumi) and Sasanian Persia / Rome
properties.highlights: Zenith of Sanskrit literature (Kalidasa), mathematics (Aryabhata, discovery of zero/decimal system), metallurgy (Iron Pillar of Delhi), and founding of Nalanda Mahavihara.

properties.name: Delhi Sultanate (Tughlaq & Khalji Dynasties)
properties.capital: Delhi (Qila Rai Pithora / Siri / Tughlaqabad) & Daulatabad
properties.ruler_or_system: Alauddin Khalji & Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Zenith expansion)
properties.primary_rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Indus, Narmada, Tapi, Krishna
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Outlines show maximum territorial reach of Sultanate garrisons and provincial governors (iqtas) prior to regional fragmentation.
properties.citation: Irfan Habib, Peter Jackson (The Delhi Sultanate), Ziauddin Barani (Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi)
properties.trade_connections: Silk routes via Central Asia, maritime connections across Arabian Sea and Persian Gulf
properties.highlights: Indo-Islamic architectural synthesis (Qutb complex, Alai Darwaza), introduction of paper, spinning wheel, monetization through silver tanka and copper jital.

properties.name: Mughal Empire (Akbar to Aurangzeb Zenith)
properties.primary_rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Indus, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Boundaries follow the 21 Subahs (provinces) mapped in Abul Fazl's Ain-i-Akbari and later Deccan annexations up to 1707.
properties.citation: Irfan Habib (An Atlas of the Mughal Empire, Oxford University Press)
properties.trade_connections: Global textile exporter producing ~25% of world industrial output (calicoes, muslins, spices)
properties.highlights: Monumental architecture (Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb, Fatehpur Sikri), standardized silver rupee, revenue assessment under Raja Todar Mal.

properties.name: Maratha Confederacy (Hindavi Swarajya & Peshwa Expansion)
properties.ruler_or_system: Chhatrapati Sovereignty & Peshwa / Sardar Confederation (Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad, Bhonsle)
properties.primary_rivers: Godavari, Krishna, Narmada, Tapi, Chambal, Mahanadi
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: APPROXIMATE SCHOLARLY RECONSTRUCTION: Depicts the direct administrative dominions (Swarajya) and Chauth / Sardeshmukhi tributary collection zones at the zenith prior to the Third Battle of Panipat (1761).
properties.citation: Stewart Gordon (The Marathas 1600-1818, Cambridge University Press) & Jadunath Sarkar
properties.trade_connections: West coast ports (Kalyan, Chaul, Vijaydurg) and inland Deccan-Gangetic caravan routes
properties.highlights: Naval power under Kanhoji Angre, light cavalry guerrilla tactics (Ganimi Kava), extensive hill fort architecture across the Western Ghats.

properties.name: British Indian Empire & Princely States
properties.ruler_or_system: Crown Rule (Viceroy & Governor-General) + ~565 Princely States under Subsidiary Alliances
properties.primary_rivers: Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Irrawaddy
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: HISTORICAL ADMINISTRATIVE BOUNDARIES: Dual political structure consisting of directly ruled British Presidencies and sovereign Indian Princely States (Sanad treaties under Crown suzerainty).
properties.citation: The Imperial Gazetteer of India (Atlas Volume, 1909) & Survey of India Historical Archives
properties.trade_connections: Extensive broad-gauge railway network, major steamship ports (Bombay, Calcutta, Madras, Karachi)
properties.highlights: Construction of the Indian Railway network (1853), telegraph lines, Survey of India Great Trigonometrical Survey under Lambton & Everest, codification of Indian Penal Code.

properties.name: Independence & Partition of India (1947)
properties.ruler_or_system: Constituent Assembly of India / Dominion of India (Governor-General & Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru)
properties.primary_rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Narmada
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: HISTORICAL DEMARCATION: Depicts the Radcliffe Line awards in Punjab and Bengal along with the initial accession of 560+ Princely States into the Indian Union orchestrated by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
properties.citation: Indian Independence Act 1947 (10 & 11 Geo. 6. c. 30) & White Paper on Indian States (1950)
properties.trade_connections: National transport integration, resettlement corridors, national highway planning
properties.highlights: Birth of the independent sovereign nation (August 15, 1947), integration of Junagadh, Hyderabad (Operation Polo), and Jammu & Kashmir into the Republic.

properties.name: Linguistic States Reorganisation (1956)
properties.ruler_or_system: Republic of India (14 States & 6 Union Territories)
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: OFFICIAL CONSTITUTIONAL BOUNDARIES: Based on the States Reorganisation Act 1956 implementing recommendations of the Fazal Ali Commission replacing complex colonial Part A, B, C, D states with cohesive linguistic federations.
properties.citation: Ministry of Law & Justice / The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Act No. 37 of 1956)
properties.trade_connections: Five-Year Plan developmental industrial corridors, Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud, DVC multipurpose dams
properties.highlights: Creation of linguistic states (Andhra Pradesh, Mysore, Kerala, Madras, Bombay State, Madhya Pradesh), landmark foundation for modern federal cooperative governance.

properties.name: Republic of India — New States of 2000
properties.ruler_or_system: Parliamentary Federal Republic (Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh & Jharkhand created)
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: Sovereign boundaries of the Republic of India per Survey of India. External boundary is essentially unchanged from 1956; only internal state reorganisation differs.
properties.citation: Survey of India / States Reorganisation & subsequent Acts
properties.trade_connections: Modern pan-India transport corridors and maritime trade
properties.highlights: Creation of Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand (2000).

properties.name: Republic of India — Bifurcation of Telangana (2014)
properties.ruler_or_system: Parliamentary Federal Republic (Telangana carved from Andhra Pradesh)
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: Sovereign boundaries of the Republic of India per Survey of India. External boundary is essentially unchanged from 1956; only internal state reorganisation differs.
properties.citation: Survey of India / States Reorganisation & subsequent Acts
properties.trade_connections: Modern pan-India transport corridors and maritime trade

properties.name: Republic of India (Present Day)
properties.ruler_or_system: Parliamentary Federal Republic — 28 States & 8 Union Territories
properties.scholarly_disclaimer: Sovereign boundaries of the Republic of India per Survey of India. External boundary is essentially unchanged from 1956; only internal state reorganisation differs.
properties.citation: Survey of India / States Reorganisation & subsequent Acts
properties.trade_connections: Modern pan-India transport corridors and maritime trade
properties.highlights: 28 States and 8 Union Territories; sovereign baseline per Survey of India.
